key_insight: Inequality may depend not just on who has access to AI agents, but also on how capable those agents are and how many each person can use. This paper develops a conceptual framework for examining these potential divides.
problem_solved: Addresses the need to identify and study how unequal access to AI agents—and differences in their quality and number—could create or deepen societal inequality.
method: Develops a conceptual framework for identifying potential sources of agentic inequality.
Examines differences in AI-agent access, quality, and number.
Proposes a research agenda to understand and address the resulting societal challenges.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the paper highlights why access, capability, and deployment scale should be considered alongside technical performance. These dimensions offer a starting point for evaluating the distributional implications of agent systems.
visual_elements: Three-axis diagram showing access, agent quality, and number of agents as dimensions of inequality.
Side-by-side illustration of people with no agent, one basic agent, and multiple advanced agents.
Conceptual flowchart linking unequal agent resources to potential societal disparities.
Research roadmap connecting sources of inequality, open questions, and possible responses.
paper_authors: Matthew Sharp, Omer Bilgin, Iason Gabriel, Lewis Hammond
